title: bug: the VS Code board's left arrow never moves a WORKING, REVIEW or DONE card: on WORKING (and Task Detail's Previous) it asks /ws for WORKING to AWAITING_APPROVAL, which is always refused (twin of the DONE JetBrains fix e44a8daf), and on REVIEW/DONE it calls prompt(), which the webview sandbox answers with null
description:
Filed by defect hunt 11-03 #5 (task-b7332618). VS Code twin of task-e44a8daf (JetBrains fix 8be13403), plus the same arrow's REVIEW/DONE branch, which is dead for a VS Code-only reason.

PROBLEM
1. WORKING card.
- board.js:364 orders the columns BACKLOG, PLANNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL, WORKING, REVIEW, DONE.
- board.js:995 shows the left arrow on every card with statusIdx > 0.
- navTask (board.js:1152-1155) posts `updateTaskStatus` with `workflowOrder[idx - 1]`. For WORKING that is AWAITING_APPROVAL.
- The post goes BoardViewProvider.ts:99 → MoeDaemonClient.ts:1160 → UPDATE_TASK.
- /ws judges the move by set_task_status's own table (WebSocketServer.ts:496-504). setTaskStatus.ts:51 reads `WORKING: ['REVIEW', 'PLANNING', 'BACKLOG', 'BLOCKED']`, so /ws replies ERROR.
- The client only logs the ERROR (MoeDaemonClient.ts:2132). The board's onError acts on APPROVE_TASK refusals only (BoardViewProvider.ts:40-46). So the click does nothing visible.
- Task Detail's Previous does the same: TaskDetailPanel.ts:540 has its own workflowOrder, and :566-567 calls `updateTaskStatus(this.taskId, workflowOrder[idx - 1])`.

2. REVIEW or DONE card.
- navTask (board.js:1147-1151) calls `prompt('Reason for reopening:')` inside the webview.
- VS Code's webview frames are sandboxed without allow-modals: microsoft/vscode main 73db368c, src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/webviewElement.ts:430 and pre/index.html:1078-1086. Local copies are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-b733/.
- In such a document prompt() returns null without showing anything (HTML Standard, "cannot show simple dialogs"). So this arrow never reopens anything.
- TaskDetailPanel.ts:555 already asks for the reopen reason host-side, with vscode.window.showInputBox.

EVIDENCE
All runs are on 19d5e67a (the moe/work-2026-10-24 tip, past 585fedc6), in snapshots outside the checkout. The re-run recipe is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-b733/notes.md.

- moe-vscode, the production media/board.js under node:vm:
    NODE_PATH=/mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-vscode/node_modules node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/zz-hunt-b733-board.test.cjs
  B1 is `not ok`. The WORKING card renders data-direction="prev", and the arrow posts `[{"type":"updateTaskStatus","taskId":"task-w","status":"AWAITING_APPROVAL"}]`.
  C2 is `not ok`. With the sandbox's answers, the arrow on a REVIEW card posts nothing (`reopenPosts: 0`). (board.output.txt)

- daemon: copy zzHuntB733WorkingPrev.test.ts into packages/moe-daemon/src/server/ and run `npx vitest run src/server/zzHuntB733WorkingPrev.test.ts`. Result: 1 passed.
  It sends the board's exact frame for a WORKING task, {type:'UPDATE_TASK', payload:{taskId, updates:{status:'AWAITING_APPROVAL'}}}. The reply is ERROR 'Cannot move task from WORKING to AWAITING_APPROVAL. Allowed: REVIEW, PLANNING, BACKLOG, BLOCKED', and the task stays WORKING.

- Chromium: headless Chrome on modal-probe.html, which nests VS Code's two sandbox token lists.
  modal-probe.dom.txt: RESULT {"deleteConfirm":false,"archiveConfirm":false,"reopenPrompt":null}
  modal-probe.stderr.txt: "Ignored call to 'prompt()'. The document is sandboxed, and the 'allow-modals' keyword is not set."

FIX DIRECTION
Use one "previous move" rule on both surfaces, mirroring JetBrains BoardMoves.previous (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/BoardMoves.kt, 8be13403):
- WORKING and AWAITING_APPROVAL → PLANNING;
- PLANNING → BACKLOG;
- REVIEW and DONE → reopen;
- anything else (BACKLOG, BLOCKED, ARCHIVED, unknown) → no left arrow.
Every status target must be in setTaskStatus.ts VALID_TRANSITIONS[from]. The WORKING arrow skips the AWAITING_APPROVAL column on purpose, because /ws refuses that move; say so in a comment.

Collect the reopen reason host-side. The webview posts only the intent (the taskId). BoardViewProvider then asks with vscode.window.showInputBox and calls reopenTask only for a non-blank answer, the same as TaskDetailPanel.ts:555. Remove prompt() from board.js.

FILES
- moe-vscode/media/board.js: navTask and the left-arrow visibility at :995 only.
- moe-vscode/src/providers/BoardViewProvider.ts: its 'reopenTask' case only.
- moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts: the 'prev'/'next' message case only.
- one new moe-vscode/tests/*.test.cjs.

Hunk ownership, so no dependsOn is needed:
- The sibling hunt row for the board's Delete and Done-column clear owns board.js's card-menu Delete, archiveDone and the clear-button markup, plus BoardViewProvider's deleteTask and archiveDoneTasks cases.
- task-e9a25fbf owns TaskDetailPanel.ts renderSteps.

The gate snapshot must be the full tree: mem:gotcha-vscode-tests-need-full-repo-snapshot.
definitionOfDone: The board's left arrow and Task Detail's Previous send UPDATE_TASK status PLANNING for a WORKING or AWAITING_APPROVAL task, and BACKLOG for a PLANNING task. No status either control can send falls outside packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/setTaskStatus.ts VALID_TRANSITIONS[from]. BACKLOG and BLOCKED cards render no left arrow.

The left arrow on a REVIEW or DONE card reaches the extension host. The host asks for the reason with vscode.window.showInputBox and sends REOPEN_TASK only for a non-blank answer. `grep -n "prompt(" moe-vscode/media/board.js` prints nothing.

A new moe-vscode node test runs the production media/board.js (under node:vm), BoardViewProvider.ts and TaskDetailPanel.ts (transpiled) for those cases and passes. `npm ci && npm test && npm run compile` passes in moe-vscode in a full-repo git-archive snapshot outside the checkout.

comments.content:
Hunt #5 clarification (architect-24611a0a, 17:28Z). The "sibling hunt row for the board's Delete and Done-column clear" in FILES is task-8b7f9560. It owns board.js's card-menu Delete, archiveDone and the clear-button markup, plus BoardViewProvider's deleteTask and archiveDoneTasks cases. This row owns navTask, the left-arrow visibility (board.js:995) and the 'reopenTask' case. The hunks are distinct, so both rows can run in parallel.

The hunt repro's C2 case covers both rows at once: clearPosts belongs to task-8b7f9560, reopenPosts to this row. Treat it as evidence only, not as this row's DoD test.
